summary: Sunnyvale sits at the heart of Silicon Valley's job gravity well — Apple, Google, Lockheed Martin, Juniper Networks, and Amazon all operate major campuses within or immediately adjacent to city limits, meaning a layoff here doesn't necessarily require a moving truck. The city's 22.8 square miles spread across the flat southern reach of the San Francisco Bay plain, where the horizon line is dominated not by hills but by the Santa Cruz Mountains to the west, visible on clear evenings and reachable within a 30-minute drive for real trail running. Downtown Murphy Avenue offers a genuine pedestrian-scale strip of restaurants, coffee shops, and sidewalk dining that gives the city a surprising pocket of identity — but step a few blocks away and you're back in the wide-lot, single-story suburban grid bisected by multi-lane arterials like El Camino Real and US-101, which fragment the city into compartments you drive between rather than walk. At a median home price of $1.82 million against a median household income of roughly $182K, the price-to-income ratio lands near 10:1 — extraordinary even by Bay Area standards, meaning buying requires either substantial existing assets or dual high-earning households. Renters face $3,065/month medians, which at least tracks more proportionally to local incomes. The weather is genuinely superb: 9.5 hours of daily sunshine, mild year-round highs near 71°F, and negligible humidity make the flat terrain more forgivable. Sunnyvale is essentially a place where the professional infrastructure is world-class and the urban fabric is aggressively ordinary — a tension that defines daily life far more than any marketing brochure admits.
